Let’s talk about something that really gets to the heart of it all—Chapter 10, Living the Radical Experiment.
Here’s the challenge: step out of your comfort zone and step into a life that’s shaped by radical faith. Imagine this as an invitation, not to be perfect, but just to try—really try—to put the teachings of Jesus into action in real, everyday ways. It’s about taking a risk and seeing what unfolds.
Picture a group of friends who decided to take this on together. They made a commitment: to pray for people all around the world, to dig deep into the words of Jesus, to give in ways that actually cost them something, to serve right where they lived, and to look for chances to go where they were needed most.
Over the course of that year, they went through all kinds of moments—some full of joy, others that were tough or even frustrating. But they also found these deep connections, both with each other and with the people they served. By the time the year was up, their lives had shifted. They discovered new priorities, built stronger relationships, and found a renewed sense of purpose.
You know, most of us don’t realize just how much can change in a single year. This experiment isn’t about ticking off boxes or following some strict formula. It’s really about opening yourself up to being changed—about letting go of what feels safe, so you can find out what’s truly possible.
The journey looks different for everyone, but the invitation is always the same: take a step, trust, and see where it leads.
So, as this chapter wraps up, it’s worth asking—what would your own experiment look like? The path isn’t easy, and you’ll face some challenges along the way. But honestly, that’s the only way you’ll ever experience the fullness of faith.
